item.title: Socialist House nominee's radical law-and-order vision: 'What are illegals?'
item.description: Chris Rabb questioned the premise of "illegal immigrants" and claimed 99% of police work does not involve pursuing criminals in a heated exchange.
item.content:encoded:
The socialist Democrat poised to represent most of Philadelphia in Congress questioned the premise of "illegal immigrants" and claimed "99%" of police work does not involve pursuing criminals.

Pennsylvania State Rep. Chris Rabb, D-West Oak Lane, made a name for himself in Harrisburg by championing progressive proposals such as abolishing the death penalty and transitioning Pennsylvania to 100% renewable energy by 2050. In 2019, Rabb introduced a "carbon pricing" bill to tax greenhouse-gas emissions above a certain cap, saying the revenue would be reinvested to help low-income consumers and support workers "displaced" from a shrunken fossil fuel industry. He also claims the "Nakba" (Palestinian displacement during the 1948 Arab-Israeli War) has "never ended."

"Raab's platform is comprised of pretty far-left, radical positions," said Fox News host Sean Hannity on "Hannity."

SOCIALIST VICTORIES SHOW DEMS' DESCENT DOWN 'DEADLY PATH OF COMMUNISM,' JOHNSON WARNS

"Among them, he advocates for Medicare for All, universal basic income, federal jobs guarantees — the government does so well educating your kids — guaranteed housing, universal childcare, government grocery stores [and] replacement of [GDP] with a so-called ‘genuine progress indicator’…," Hannity listed.

"In other words, what he is saying is he would not just reshape our institutions, he would tear them down, fundamentally transform them in what I believe would be a very dangerous way."

Rabb pushed back on some of the characterizations, telling Hannity in the case of the DSA’s effort to abolish the Senate, "that’s not what I’m running on."

When Hannity asked whether Rabb — who boasts of running in the "bluest district in America" — truly supports "amnesty for illegals" and abolishing national borders, the lawmaker replied: "What are illegals?"

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

Hannity responded, "Illegal immigrants: people that didn't respect our laws, borders, and sovereignty; entered the country without permission."

Rabb said he didn’t accept the "premise" of the question.

"There are folks who have documentation. But these are not criminal acts," he said, adding that he "absolutely" wants to abolish ICE and "dismantle immigrant concentration camps."

"I want to end all deportations. We want to make sure that there's an immigration system that is fair, just, and efficient, and we don't have that system," Rabb added. He went on to cite an immigration reform package led by Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., and former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema, D-Ariz., that he lamented "your president" successfully killed.

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

When asked about abolishing police as an institution — in line with socialist doctrine — Rabb said the statement was "interesting" because there were few or no organized police departments in early America.

"Long before there was any notion of policing, we had Founders that did not even understand that term. Policing is something that's evolved over time," Rabb said.

"Ultimately, what we want is to have communities that are safe, and 99% of what police do are not going after the bad guys," he said.

Philadelphia did not organize the PPD as a centralized municipal force until 1854. Before that, local elected constables and civilian watchmen patrolled their neighborhoods for crime. The PPD formed after a series of riots, when what is now Philadelphia was divided between the City of Philadelphia and Philadelphia County, which are now coterminous.

173 HOUSE DEMOCRATS VOTE AGAINST RESOLUTION HONORING POLICE AMID RISING ATTACKS

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"We need to keep our communities safe and there were ways of doing that before the term ‘police’ ever existed," Rabb said.

On disarming police, a policy some socialists support, Rabb said he believes in "arming oneself," arguing that, as someone with Southern ancestry, the only way his family could protect themselves was through self-defense.

"We couldn’t trust the police because they were largely part of the [Ku Klux] Klan," Rabb said. His paternal family roots trace to Columbus, Miss.

Rabb upset the Democratic establishment in his May primary, defeating state Sen. Sharif Street, D-North Philadelphia — the son of popular former Mayor John Street — who also had the backing of incumbent Mayor Cherelle Parker and former Gov. Edward Rendell.

No Republicans vied for the nomination, leaving Rabb reportedly facing only independent Dennis Mahoney in November.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rabb for comment.

item.title: Trump says White House ballroom ruling jeopardizes lives of future presidents, vows Supreme Court appeal
item.description: Trump vows an immediate Supreme Court appeal after a federal appeals court ordered construction halted on his "massive" White House ballroom project.
item.content:encoded:
After a panel of federal judges ordered construction on the White House ballroom to stop, President Donald Trump said he will immediately appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

In a Truth Social post on Friday, Trump decried the 2-1 decision from the the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit as "horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful."

"The Circuit Court’s decision, which is totally wrong on the vital subject of STANDING, of which the plaintiff has none, severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House — including all future Presidents of the United States, and their families, as well as the lives of all those visiting, such as Heads of State and other Dignitaries, and all Americans who wish to visit the historic, beautiful Executive Mansion," Trump wrote in the post.

He also accused the court of refusing to acknowledge that the ballroom, which he said is being built ahead of schedule and under budget, "is a Gift from President Trump and Great Patriots of the United States of America."

TRUMP WARNS JUDGE AGAINST SACRIFICING NATIONAL SECURITY BY BLOCKING WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM, DRONE BASE

"There will be no expense to the American Taxpayer. This unjust decision must be overturned by the Supreme Court in its entirety," Trump wrote.

The appeals court on Friday upheld a lower-court decision that paused above-ground construction of the proposed 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom project, which replaced the demolished East Wing.

The earlier ruling allowed work to continue on underground national-security facilities and certain safety and security measures, a decision the higher court also upheld.

The appeals court said in its 136-page ruling that the decision to build a "massive ballroom" lies with Congress, not with the executive branch.

REPUBLICANS EYE PICKING UP $400M TAB FOR TRUMP'S BALLROOM AS SOME DEMS OPEN TO 'DISCUSS' IDEA

Judges Patricia Millett and Brad Garcia wrote the majority opinion, remarking that there is no precedent for what Trump has done.

"We are aware of no instance in American history in which a President unilaterally and using privately collected funds demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now," they wrote.

The judges said their ruling does not prevent the president from building the ballroom if it is authorized by Congress in the future.

As Trump pointed out in his social media post, the ruling was stayed for 14 days to allow the defendants to seek a Supreme Court review.

It is not immediately clear if the Supreme Court will take up this case.

item.title: Blackjack losses, a chilling phone call and a diverted flight cap a chaotic Las Vegas vacation
item.description: David Hookstead's Las Vegas trip featured high-limit blackjack tables, Golden Tiki, Stage Door and machine guns while navigating threats in Las Vegas.
item.content:encoded:
*NOTE: Some names, locations, techniques and information have been withheld due to their sensitive nature.

You often don’t realize you’re in a fight for your soul until you’re deep in it.

As my loyal readers and viewers have realized, I have been fairly off the grid for roughly the past week.

Why?

It was time for my annual trip to Las Vegas, but unlike previous trips, this one was happening with the looming threat of the Iran War, death threats and the IRGC. Things were different for this working-class man this time around.

While I’m not going to get into specifics, there’s no question that due to a heightened alert status and ever-evolving threat matrices, precautions that never had been taken before were going to be necessary. It turns out some people aren’t fans of my outspoken ways, and unlike people who claim to be "threatened" by blue hair liberals (literally comical to even consider dangerous), being under the threat from a state-backed actor is a totally different ball game.

No box could go unchecked.

The first decision that was made was that I would move to the airport under the cover of darkness.

There are a couple of reasons why this was deemed the best option. First, it allows me to move when the city and airport aren’t buzzing yet.

Second, the streets being mostly empty provide far more tactical advantages than if they’re crowded and something goes wrong.

The plan didn’t survive me making it to the front door.

Immediately upon exiting the Hookstead Compound (location classified) with my bags, I spotted two military-age males that I’d never seen before. Keep in mind the entire point of the movements and schedule is that NOBODY is supposed to be around.

I know enough about the people who live in my vicinity to recognize most of them. I’ve never seen these two men in my life. It’s a shocking sight to behold, but they’re way more shocked to see me than vice versa.

A decision had to be made in a half of a second over whether or not this was finally it. Would the entire operation be aborted before entering the vehicle for the airport?

LUCKY TRAVELER WINS $3.3M JACKPOT ON 'WHEEL OF FORTUNE' SLOT MACHINE AT HARRY REID INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

Ultimately, sometimes the only way to fix a problem is to go clean through it (another lesson that some people would be wise to follow for Iran).

I closed the space quickly, deemed the two men not an immediate threat showing hostile intent and got on the move as quickly as possible.

As planned, the streets are completely empty and we’re able to get into the airport without issues. From that point, the goal was simple:

Blend in as much as possible, go unnoticed and get seated on the plane as quickly as possible. Every minute spent in the open at the airport is a minute where nobody is in complete control of the situation. That’s far from ideal.

Little did I know things would only get stranger from here.

I chose a seat as close to the cockpit as possible. Unusual for someone with my blue-collar roots? For sure, but a necessity given the stakes.

What seemed like a routine and normal flight became very different in a matter of seconds. For the first time in my life, I was on a plane where a metal gate was closed off up front by the cockpit without explanation.

That’s right.

There was a metal gate rolled out making the front portion of the plane an impenetrable fortress. I tried to get a look past the gate, but found it difficult. My only guess was that one of the pilots was out of the cockpit for some reason, but I was never able to confirm that.

Fortunately, the plane touched down without further incident.

The working-class man’s Las Vegas vacation was underway.

Just as quickly as I’d gotten on the plane to Vegas, I disappeared into the crowd blending in again. Nobody knows me, and I don’t know them. The less attention the better. We’re not chasing clout. We’re chasing demons that have haunted us for a long time, and doing it while operating to survive.

Things were about to get weird (noticing a trend) very quickly.

My driver appeared like a normal woman attempting to make small talk.

It was anything but normal.

For some unexplained reason, this woman starts talking to me about sex and a sex museum. At one point, she starts asking if I like sex.

Am I on a hidden camera show? Am I being pranked? I start making very measured and careful statements assuming whatever I say is absolutely being recorded. I can’t wait to get the hell out of this taxi as soon as possible. A working-class man might not have much in life, but we do have one thing:

Common sense, and common sense dictates asking a stranger about sex in a vehicle is about as strange as it gets.

I get out at the Cosmopolitan in Las Vegas with one clear goal in mind:

Get to the blackjack table as quickly as I can.

I dumped my stuff into my room, which for a working-class guy who had to fight for everything in life, I can tell you was pretty shocking. It featured a massive bedroom, a living room area, huge walk-in shower, a hot tub and a balcony overlooking Las Vegas.

I’m not going to lie to you all. It was epic. I guess life occasionally hands the downtrodden a win in life.

To the tables I went.

I pulled out a roll of working-class money and set it down at a blackjack table in the high-limit room. Now, some of you might be asking, "David, what is a guy like you doing in the high-limit room? That doesn’t seem like it’s your speed."

Fair question, and the answer is simple:

Privacy.

The high-limit room at the Cosmo is one of the nicest in Las Vegas, and it’s also fairly secluded.

Remember, I have significant threats I have to worry about, and unlike the unhinged clowns roaming around, the people who want me dead actually have the means to carry it out.

Head on a swivel.

I sit down at a double-deck table, and immediately go on a nice little run earning more money in a matter of minutes than a regular working-class guy does over the course of a few weeks.

When you don’t come from much, you know when to walk away with the win the universe gifted you (this energy won’t last for long). I push back from the table for the time being and keep the operation rolling.

Next stop? Stage Door for a hot dog and a cheap beer. The hot dog, while not amazing, is certainly worth the money and it’s also a tradition. It hits the spot, and I soon get word a second seasoned Las Vegas operator has arrived. For the sake of the story, he is identified as VO2. VO1, another seasoned Las Vegas operator, won’t arrive until the next day.

From here, things progress rather normally. We hit up the arts district for a couple beers and did a little exploring.

I was about to hit my next unexpected hurdle, and while I’m on a high alert status, I didn’t see this kind of roadblock coming.

I decide to head back for some more high-limit blackjack, and am promptly informed the casino needs extra information from me. I’m not going to share the specific information in a public setting, but it appears the amount of working-class money that I’ve put on the table in one day has possibly triggered some money laundering tripwires.

Me? The working-class guy from rural Wisconsin? You have to be kidding me.

After a brief conversation with the casino bosses, it’s smoothed over and the gambling continues.

Remember the win I had early in the day? That’s wiped out in about an hour, and then go ahead and tack on a few paychecks on top of that.

Now, this is where most people would start panicking. Those kinds of swings at the tables break most people, but most people aren’t from my rural Wisconsin background.

I’m in the fight, and while the IRGC hasn’t taken its shot yet, the casino is drawing financial blood.

Just like knowing when to walk away when you win, you also need to know when to not chase losses. I cut the cord, push back and live to fight another day.

I grab a burger on my way back to the room, crush it and pass out as soon as my head hits the pillow.

Day two started like any other day in Las Vegas. All was quiet in the streets and casinos and people were still asleep by the time I was on the move with enough caffeine in my system to kill a rhino. I guess I’m just built differently. If chugging Celsius was a skill, I’d be the Tom Brady of getting it done.

The day started with biscuits and gravy at Ellis Island, followed by getting kicked in the shorts at the blackjack tables. Fortunately, the losses this time around aren’t nearly as vicious, but it’s still not great. I’m now deep in a gambling hole. Not great, but it’s only a loss once you actually leave the city.

What happened next nobody could see coming…….most of all me.

The bat phone buzzes to life, and I see a name that stops me dead in my tracks. I know something serious must be happening for me to be receiving this call, and I now have a major issue:

I can’t take this call outside of a completely secure location.

My hotel room, which would get the job done, is too far away and time is of critical importance.

The decision is made for VO2 and myself to relocate to a closer secure location, and with the doorway secure, I answer the phone.

A serious flow of information starts flooding in.

Seconds feel like hours.

There are times when years pass without anything happening, and then there are times where decisions are made in seconds that can change everything.

This is the latter.

I try to process the information as quickly and as efficiently as I can, and it ultimately boils down to one call:

Go or don’t go.

You could hear a pin drop in the secure room. Based on the information I was hearing, I simply was not confident with going.

It’s a no go with the door left open for a decision to be made at a later time.

With my head spinning with a million thoughts, I get word that VO1 has touched down and is on his way to the rendezvous point. After a brief conversation, we head over to Ole Red (Blake Shelton’s establishment) for nachos and a beer.

The nachos were absolute fire. The best nachos I’ve ever had? No, but definitely very solid and delicious with some added brisket.

Next up was Golden Tiki in the Chinatown area of Las Vegas. Golden Tiki is another tradition every single year for us. It’s an outstanding tiki bar with a unique vibe, and some bathroom wallpaper that is a bit shocking at first sight. Seeing as how this is a family website, I won’t share further details. I have myself a couple tiki drinks, and both are well worth the money.

As a working-class guy, I can really only afford cheap domestic beers, but this is vacation. Let’s live a little. Plus, with the death threats, I simply can’t be living for the future. Much like fighting the demons, any day could be the last, and we’re leaving it all out on the field.

Now, there is one location in Las Vegas I’ve been more than eager to get to, and with the full trio locked in, it’s time to execute the plan.

Hogs & Heifers.

For those of you who don’t know, Hogs is an absolutely insane Las Vegas institution. It’s not for the faint of heart or easily offended. It’s a bar for true American patriots and it has the most entertaining bartenders in Vegas by orders of magnitude. They’ll insult you in the most vulgar way possible, but it’s all in the name of good fun.

It was closed last year, and that was the first time since discovering the gem that we weren’t able to go. That needed to change and it did.

It’s now located at the Plaza while its new permanent home is built.

The bartenders were as rowdy and fun as ever. While it’s an outpost location, it felt just like the old Hogs so many have come to know and love, and the Coors Banquets were as cold as ever.

Oh, did I mention the insults and jabs were flying in all directions? It felt good to be back, and as always, you meet some insane characters in there.

We rotate between playing blackjack and hopping in and out of the bar as the day stabilizes following the phone call in the secure location.

I’m actually feeling fairly good about it as I head back to my hotel room, but I’m also starving. I order room service and get hit with one hell of a surprise:

The full room service experience is a $160 minimum spend.

I honestly think what I’m hearing can’t possibly be true. I’m trying to order a wrap. I don’t need the full room service experience. Bring it to me in a bag and a plastic container and I’ll be fine. That’s exactly what ended up happening.

How is a working-class guy supposed to be able to afford a $160 minimum spend? It’s simply not possible. We’re lucky just to have food on the table. Forget the fancy stuff. Save that for the millionaires and billionaires, not guys like myself.

First, I have to operate under new procedures thanks to the Iranians. Second, I am gutted at the table. Third, I am reminded of just how blue-collar I am when ordering room service. The losses keep piling up.

Having said that, the wrap was delicious and the portion sizes were excellent.

Tuesday started just like any other day. I filmed a short war update and crushed a couple Celsius cans, and the vibes were high.

I’m also very excited for one very simple reason:

The schedule has a portion blocked off for letting it rip with some machine guns.

Generally speaking, I hate indoor shooting ranges and shooting ranges in general. I had a private outdoor one at my house growing up, and the idea of strangers with guns around me at a range has never been something I’ve really enjoyed. I know how good I am with a gun (most working-class men from Wisconsin can say the same), but I don’t know how good these random people are or what stupid stuff they might do. Add in the fact foreign tourists don’t know an AK-47 from a Beretta M9, and I think you get the point.

Well, when in Vegas, you do things you don’t do at home. I grabbed a PKM machine gun and PPSh-41 Soviet submachine gun.

Both were absolutely awesome. The PKM was shockingly light, and the rate of fire was exceptional.

The PPSh-41 was cool mostly because it’s the submachine gun the Soviets used in WWII against the Germans.

I wouldn’t say it’s a particularly impressive submachine gun or special, but it can’t be beat from a historical standpoint if you’re looking for foreign WWII guns. I can’t recommend both enough if you ever get a chance to shoot them. You won’t regret it. We also met some cool Welsh dudes at the range who absolutely loved America. It was a humbling reminder just how good we have it here in the USA. Foreigners would give anything to be part of our club, and none of us would give it up for anything.

Next, the trio filed over to El Cortez where I had a very mediocre bratwurst before, yet again, getting my wallet crushed at the blackjack tables.

I hope my wife is okay being solely responsible for the bills for the foreseeable future because this has turned into a catastrophic gambling nightmare.

What do you do when the world is against you and the demons are starting to sing? You numb the pain with a little Coors Banquet, and that’s exactly what we did by swinging by Hogs, where the bartenders were in rare form. I say that as a compliment. I can’t wait to visit next year once it’s in its final home. I can only imagine how glorious it will be.

The day wound down with a stop in the Arts District for a delicious espresso martini and some insanely good Mexican food, followed by a short stop at Ellis Island before closing beers at Stage Door. I eventually found myself back in the high-limit room with my blue-collar money (no money laundering concerns this time) and actually came out a little ahead. Slowly but surely, I’m crawling out of the hole I created.

However, my winning wasn’t the highlight of day three coming to an end. The dude sitting next to me at the table was hysterical. I legit couldn’t stop chuckling at every word coming out of this guy’s mouth, and a woman (I believe girlfriend but can’t say for sure) shows up and sits down next to him. Turns out she’s a former golf superstar and was at one point one of the top golfers in the world. Admittedly, I have no idea who she is, but I also couldn’t recognize any golfer other than maybe three or four. That’s a sport for rich people, and I’m anything but wealthy, no matter what the rumor mill says.

They were both a ton of fun, and then a Canadian showed up ripping cigs. What a night at the high-limit blackjack table. I wouldn’t have cared if I lost every penny because the dude was so funny that it made the whole thing entertaining, no matter the outcome. Fairly certain I also saw him tip several thousand dollars to the dealers in the time I was with him.

Day four was the final full day in Las Vegas, and after breakfast and some more blackjack, we decided to catch a ride to Fremont.

We’re not 50 yards down the street when the right front tire of the vehicle blows out, and the driver declares an emergency. It’s in the worst possible location. We’re nowhere near a parking garage or the safety of a building.

Is this how it ends for me? Have plans been set in motion that can’t be stopped?

I don’t know and I’m definitely not going to wait to find out. VO1 and I bail out of the vehicle, and I start scanning in all directions for threats. I don’t see anything, but we’re completely in the open and exposed. Nowhere to run. Nowhere to hide. I took a look at the guy’s vehicle, and as VO1 noted, "His right tire is f****d."

I peered over, and assessed the situation.

His right tire was completely destroyed. I don’t even understand what happened. I never heard a pop or any kind of blast.

It was fine when we entered the vehicle, and it was anything but fine now. Every second matters. The longer we stay exposed, the more risk we’re assuming.

A backup vehicle - a big black SUV - whisks in and we’re in it without hesitation racing towards where we’re going.

I still have absolutely no idea what happened with the original vehicle, and I doubt I ever will. Some questions are best left unasked.

We grab a couple beers and attempt to win some money. VO1 pulls an absurd four card blackjack split and hits it. The craziest part is it wasn’t the first time. He did the exact same thing earlier in the day at Ellis Island.

Two successful four card splits in one trip? Good luck replicating that at any point in the near future.

I also noticed at one point in the night that my phone all of a sudden had a crack in the screen protector, which VO2 and myself found extremely odd. It was never dropped and never left alone. None of us could explain it. Maybe there was a perfectly ordinary explanation. Maybe there wasn't. Either way, it became one more strange thing on a trip that seemed determined to keep getting stranger.

Fortunately, the night didn’t feature any more unexpected surprises, and instead focused on some honest conversations about some theories we have about relationships and life. Those aren’t my stories alone to share, so I won’t out of respect for the other parties involved.

I wake up, bang out another video update for the Hookheads (what my fans call themselves on YouTube) and grab a stack of cash to hit the high-limit room one final time before leaving.

That’s when there was an unexpected change of plans.

I’m well over a thousand miles from home, and I get a call learning that my HVAC system is still not only not fixed, but getting the company to show up and do it has become a nightmare for my wife, who is running point at home.

It’s enraging. We’re now weeks into this situation without a resolution, and my patience has officially run out.

Instead of spending some blue-collar money one last time at the tables, I’m now dealing with this issue and then I run into a major computer problem.

What seemed like a successful trip is unraveling into a nightmare as I sit on the one-yard line waiting to punch the ball in.

You remember the start about a fight for your soul? I successfully avoided detection in Las Vegas (major win), clawed back some losses to an acceptable point (huge win) and was ready to roll one last time.

One final engagement at the tables.

Instead I’m in a hotel room dealing with infuriating nonsense.

It’s not the bright moments when you have to remember to save your soul. It’s the dark ones, and that’s what I’m left doing as the clock ticks down.

I eventually get enough of it smoothed out, but now I have to race to catch my plane. With a Burger King burger and some fries in my stomach, it’s time to go home.

I spent five days dancing with the demons, battling the highest stakes I’ve ever gambled and made it out alive.

Little did I know the biggest fight yet was only hours away.

In the final stretch of my plane ride home I start to notice something that I don’t think many other people are:

The plane is flying in a holding pattern.

We’re not getting any closer to our final destination. We’re holding.

A brief holding pattern is one thing. A holding pattern that carries on for an extended period of time is rarely a good thing.

Then the pilot comes over the PA system and gives us all the devastating news. The plane is being diverted to a completely different airport due to the final destination having a ground closure.

You have to be kidding me, right? I just made it out of Las Vegas alive and am supposed to be landing back home in minutes.

Instead, we’re bound for an airport much further away from my home, and while that’s bad enough, what’s looming is an experience so hellish that I can only pray I never have to repeat it again.

Once the plane lands, we’re just stuck on a runway for hours. It feels like Lord of the Flies. Discontent is growing. Now, I will say none of this is the fault of the crew. I’m not blaming them. I’m blaming the universe.

We finally pull into a parking spot…..that is nowhere near a gate. The next problem? A stairs vehicle is blocking the bus from coming to get us.

It just drags on and on. I’ve seen darkness in life. I’m not even sure what words could accurately sum up this situation. I want to be anywhere else on the planet right now.

Eventually, we get off and are unloaded in a terminal to find a way home. Absolute disaster on all levels.

I make it home and my wonderful wife has pizza waiting. It’s the small victories that really make you smile. The highest of highs. The lowest of lows. All in a span of a few days. I fought the demons and won only to be dragged back down in the closing moments. Fortunately, I was able to pry victory away from the brutal jaws of defeat.

What comes next? I don’t know, but I do know someday I will lose this fight. That day just isn’t today. We ride again at dawn. Let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

item.title: GOP senator breaks with Trump over 'woke' Smithsonian history battle
item.description: Lisa Murkowski broke with Republicans to defend the Smithsonian, writing to Doug Burgum with concerns about Trump's executive order on museum signage.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, is splitting from the majority of Republicans on the GOP's pushback against the Smithsonian Institution's teaching of American history.

The moderate Republican senator sent a letter to the Trump administration alongside Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., asking for more information on President Donald Trump's directive to install "temporary signage" outside the National Museum of American History, after he accused the museum of teaching historical accounts with an inaccurate and hyper-partisan lens.

"As Chair and Ranking Member of the Senate Interior Appropriations Subcommittee, we write to express our concern and to request more information regarding the role the Department of the Interior (DOI) will have in implementing Executive Order (EO) 14416, ‘Restoring Trust in the Smithsonian Institution,’" the letter said.

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

Republicans have heaped scrutiny on the Smithsonian Institution, which gets roughly $1 billion in taxpayer dollars from Congress annually, for exhibits that the GOP has argued are inherently political.

But Murkowski appeared to refute that in her bipartisan letter, writing to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, "For the past 180 years, the Smithsonian Institution has been committed to sharing objective historical evidence through research and education, not political narratives."

"The Smithsonian Institution has worked tirelessly to present a comprehensive narrative of our nation’s amazing history, from its many triumphs to its trials. There is nothing more American than telling our story truthfully," the senators said.

Trump signed an executive order late last month directing Burgum to utilize existing avenues "to restore trust in the Smithsonian Institution," including installing "temporary exhibits or signage on [federally owned] sidewalks, walkways, and land used by the public that corrects inaccurate information presented in the Museum."

Murkowski and Merkley are asking the administration for information on whether there's any precedent for federal land or funds being used to communicate "conflicting information" to a nearby entity's operations, who is compiling the information and what the timeline and cost of the signage will be.

Examples Republicans have seized on include an exhibit that described Disney's "Steamboat Willie" as representing "vestiges of long-standing traditions of blackface minstrelsy," while accusing the broader curation of the museum of being "anti-white" and "woke."

It's led several conservatives on the House Appropriations Committee to tell Fox News Digital they would like to see new guardrails on the Smithsonian's federal funds to force the museum to change controversial exhibits or risk losing its government dollars.

item.title: NFL great Steve Smith Sr says he has 'no damn idea' what's going on with embattled 49ers star Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: Steve Smith Sr. said he has "no damn idea" what's going on with Brandon Aiyuk, urging someone to intervene before the 49ers star self-sabotages his career.
item.content:encoded:
Carolina Panthers legend Steve Smith is of a similar mindset as many NFL fans when it comes to embattled San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk: He has "no damn idea" what’s going on.

Aiyuk’s issue with the 49ers date back to 2024, when they voided his 2026 guaranteed salary after failing to fulfill obligations regarding his rehab from the ACL injury he suffered in October 2024. He has further estranged himself from the team with bizarre social media posts over the past year.

"It's a lot of things, but man, I have no damn idea what's going on in that young man's head," Smith said during an appearance on OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"It's really unique. I was thinking about this too a few times. I just wanted to tweet something and I was like, ‘No, I will be like everyone else putting him down.’"

The five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver said there is clearly something going on with Aiyuk, and that somebody needs to step in and help the 28-year-old.

"There's clearly something going on, and I don't want to say in his head because that could come off very judgmental, but there's obviously something going on in his heart that's not aligning with what his picture is seeing of how his career is starting to go," Smith said.

"He needs to have someone in his camp needs to sit him down and ask him what is his real goal and outcome because everything he's doing right now, he is self-sabotaging himself. Because he's a hell of a football player."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

In Aiyuk’s time away from the team, he has been charged by prosecutors with the California misdemeanor offense of exhibition of speed after he filmed himself speeding on a public roadway near the 49ers facility.

He has posted Instagram Stories about playing for the Washington Commanders, and then got in a social media spat with his former Arizona State teammate, Jayden Daniels, effectively putting that possibility to rest.

Aiyuk then seemed to take classless shots at head coach Kyle Shanahan after his car accident on social media. When asked if Aiyuk will play again in the NFL, Smith said he didn’t know.

The two-time All-Pro said he hopes that Aiyuk does something to help himself before it is too late to play again in the NFL.

"We all have seen players do a lot better, a lot worse things than this, and they've still been employed. So, I don't know what's going on and I just hope that he can figure it out so he doesn't find himself in a place that he doesn't want to be, which is unemployed and looking at his career in the rearview mirror and looking at life without football through the front windshield," Smith , who spoke on behalf of Forzet.

Aiyuk seemed to be on his way to becoming one of the top wide receivers in the NFL after his 2023 season, when he recorded 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. After a drawn-out negotiations, he signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers.

He only played in seven games in 2024 before suffering his season-ending ACL injury and has not yet returned to the field while finding himself in the headlines for all the wrong reasons.

item.title: Organ harvesting began while patients still showed ‘signs of life,’ federal investigation finds
item.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says Network for Hope pressured medical personnel to proceed with organ procurement despite patients showing signs of life.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has begun the decertification of Network for Hope, the federally designated organ procurement organization serving Kentucky and parts of Indiana, Ohio and West Virginia, following federal reviews that uncovered serious patient safety failures.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services initiated the decertification action after investigations revealed persistent safety issues, including instances where the organ harvesting process was initiated on patients who still showed active signs of life.

Appearing on America's Newsroom, Dr. Marc Siegel, a senior medical analyst for Fox News, described details from his interview with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. regarding the department's actions against the nonprofit organization.

EATING TOO MUCH PROTEIN COULD BACKFIRE, EXPERTS WARN AFTER LONGEVITY REVIEW

"Health and Human Services Secretary Kennedy is bringing to light horror stories about the dark corners of organ harvesting," Siegel said.

"The department is now pulling the accreditation of Kentucky's Network for Hope, the main organ procurement organization in the state."

Network for Hope's chief executive officer stated that the organization plans to appeal the federal decision, maintaining that it remains fully compliant with organ procurement and transportation network policies.

FDA APPROVES FIRST-EVER MRNA FLU VACCINE FOR MILLIONS OF OLDER AMERICANS

Siegel said he spoke with Secretary Kennedy about the case of TJ Hoover, a prospective donor who reportedly nearly had his organs removed by Network for Hope while still alive.

"Even after those signs of life, Kennedy says the organ procurement process continued until the physician refused to proceed," the doctor said.

HHS' Health Resources and Services Administration examined 351 cases at Network for Hope between 2021 and 2024 in which organ donation was authorized but ultimately not completed.

The review identified 103 cases with concerning features, including 73 patients with what HHS described as "neurological signs incompatible with organ donation."

"HHS says it uncovered 73 separate instances where the process of harvesting an organ should have been stopped sooner," Siegel said. "The investigation revealed that the nonprofit pressured medical personnel to proceed despite patients showing active signs of live and neurological function."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

According to federal officials, investigators found evidence of inadequate neurological assessments, poor coordination with hospital care teams, questionable consent practices and improper classification of causes of death.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Thirty percent of the procedures that they were performing had something wrong with them," Siegel added. "If there's a bad organization that's willing to do things that are unethical, they're going to get away with things at any place where they operate."

Despite the agency's findings, Siegel noted that Kennedy remains supportive of organ donation when conducted under proper standards, pointing to personal experience with his own family.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Kennedy says he strongly supports organ donation when it's done ethically and properly," Siegel said. "His own nephew, Michael Hines, saved multiple lives by donating his organs after his death at age 20."

item.title: Sen Lankford accuses Pornhub of 'preying on children' in blistering letter
item.description: Sen. James Lankford accuses Pornhub of "preying on children" in a letter responding to the site's campaign against state age verification laws.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE - Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., is accusing Pornhub of "preying on children" in a sharply worded letter Friday responding to the adult website's campaign against age-verification laws, arguing the company is more concerned about protecting its customer base than shielding minors from explicit content.

In a letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Lankford rebuked Pornhub's July 28 message to state lawmakers opposing age-verification requirements, saying the company "has no interest in protecting children" and suggesting it fears losing users if minors are prevented from accessing its content.

"Pornhub preys on children," Lankford wrote in the letter directed to Solomon Friedman, a partner and the vice president of compliance for Ethical Capital Partners (ECP), the private equity firm that acquired MindGeek, the parent company of Pornhub, which has since been rebranded as Aylo.

INDIANA REPUBLICAN SENATOR MOVES TO BLOCK KIDS FROM ACCESSING PORN ONLINE

"It exposes them to horrific sexual content and does nothing to ensure that children are not sexually abused in the content it hosts," Lankford wrote. "Pornhub’s letter suggests that tech companies should be responsible for protecting children from pornography."

He continued, "Lawmakers can and should hold tech companies accountable for the harm they pose to children. But that should not preclude state and federal lawmakers from holding platforms like Pornhub accountable for the harm it causes. Pornhub’s letter fails to say the quiet part out loud: Pornhub would lose customers if children were prohibited from viewing its content."

On July 28, Pornhub sent a letter to state lawmakers shared by the Tallahassee Democrat, criticizing age-verification laws like the one in Florida, one of at least 25 states to enact such requirements.

The pornography site wrote, "We are writing to you because, as a community, we are deeply concerned about the harm being caused by the performative, ineffective, and unenforceable age verification laws you have taken part in passing despite your intention of protecting minors. Everyone subjected to these laws is more at risk than ever before of encountering online harm."

NEW MEXICO SEEKS MASSIVE PENALTY FROM META AFTER JURY FOUND TECH GIANT LIABLE FOR ENDANGERING CHILDREN

Lankford cited research from the American Psychological Association indicating the average age of first exposure to pornography among boys is 13.37 years, with some children reporting exposure as young as 5. He argued that age-verification laws are a necessary step to reduce minors' access to explicit material while rejecting Pornhub's privacy concerns as overstated.

"Age verification laws are an important piece of making the internet safer for children," Lankford wrote. "It is not the only solution to combat this problem, but it is an important start. Pornhub’s letter argues that age verification laws increase privacy risks for adults. But as you know, many state laws require platforms to delete personal information as soon as the age verification is complete."

Lankford highlighted the Supreme Court’s affirmation of age verification laws in Free Speech Coalition vs. Paxton, which found that they do not cause an undue burden for adults and that states have a duty to protect minors from pornography.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT CLEARS WAY FOR DESANTIS-BACKED LAW RESTRICTING CHILDREN AT SOME DRAG SHOWS

"Parents today face an uphill battle when it comes to protecting their children online," Lankford wrote. "Age verification is one simple step platforms can take to help preserve childhood innocence. This is especially true for platforms that host violent and perverse sexual content. Pornhub should be ashamed of its letter to state lawmakers and ashamed that they do nothing to protect children."

Fox News Digital reached out to Friedman and Pornhub for comment.

item.content:encoded:

A description of the video says, "The sensor pans to track an area of contrast from left to right across the background, keeping it generally centered within the frame. The sensor adjusts collection mode and level of magnification several times."

NASA CHIEF CONFIRMS AGENCY HAS UNEXPLAINED UFO IMAGERY: 'WE DON'T KNOW WHAT IT IS'

Assistant to the secretary of war for public affairs and chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in part of a Friday statement, "Today, the Department of War is publishing the fifth release of declassified and historical Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) files as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE)."

President Donald Trump declared in a Truth Social post earlier this year that he would call for the release of such materials.

LONG-HIDDEN UFO INFORMATION AT CENTER OF TRUMP PUSH TO FREE FORMER OFFICIALS

item.title: Rogers opens door to Democratic voters after El-Sayed’s primary victory: ‘There is still hope’
item.description: Mike Rogers appeals to Michigan Democrats after Abdul El-Sayed's primary win, saying those who feel unrepresented have a home with his campaign.
item.content:encoded:
Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers opened the door to Michigan Democrats on Friday after far-left progressive Abdul El-Sayed's primary victory, assuring them "there is still hope" and they have a "home" with his campaign.

"If you're among the majority of Democratic voters that woke up on Wednesday feeling, well, hopeless, because the person who won does not represent your values, well, just know, there is still hope," Rogers said in a video posted on X Friday.

"Michigan deserves a senator who is ready to sit with you, hear from you, and represent you."

El-Sayed narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in one of the nation's most closely watched Democratic primaries, setting up a November showdown with Rogers, who ran uncontested.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Rogers addressed Democratic voters directly, casting his campaign as a home for those who feel their values are not reflected in El-Sayed's candidacy as he tries to court the hundreds of thousands of Democrats who voted for Stevens but may not feel comfortable voting for El-Sayed.

"The parents across Michigan who want an education system that sets up their kids for success, you have a home with us," he said. "To grandparents across Michigan who are heartbroken from watching their kids and grandkids leave the state, you have a home with us. To young people who are looking for real solutions to solve our housing affordability crisis, you have a home with us. To working families who don't want higher taxes and lower paychecks, well, you have a home with us."

Rogers also accused El-Sayed's campaign of promoting "anger, divisiveness, calls for violence" and views he said are out of step with Michigan voters.

"And to the vast majority of people across Michigan who do not want to throw their support behind a campaign filled with anger, divisiveness, calls for violence, and the views that are out of touch with your values, well, you have a home with us," he said.

EL-SAYED'S THREAT AGAINST GOP RIVAL BACKFIRES AS CONSERVATIVES BRING RECEIPTS: 'IS DUBAI IN FLORIDA?'

If Rogers wins in November, Republicans would flip the seat held by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters and help protect their control of the Senate.

"Over the next 90 days, I'm going to work hard to earn your trust, to earn your support, and earn your vote," Rogers said. "We have a state to save, Michigan. Let's get to work."

Rogers' outreach to Democrats was praised by some conservatives and pundits on social media.

In a post on X, former DSA member Jake Altman wrote, "I voted for Biden. I voted for Harris. I will vote for Mike Rogers. I just donated to the campaign. This is not a time to sit on your hands. Stand up for the man who fights terrorists, not the one who sympathizes with them."

"Mike Rogers directly asks for Democrats to support him in Michigan. The majority of Michigan Democrats voted against Abdul El-Sayed. This is well done," OutKick founder Clay Travis posted on X.

In another post on X, Democrats For Mike Rogers wrote, "Mike Rogers is meeting the moment. We’re putting country over party and voting for Mike Rogers in November. It’s never been more important. We must unite and defeat the extremism of Abdul El-Sayed and his allies."

El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and former Wayne County health director who unsuccessfully ran for governor in 2018, has campaigned on Medicare-for-all and abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement. He has also been a vocal critic of Israel during its war with Hamas and has called Israel's actions in Gaza "genocide."

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: THE REPUBLICAN-LED VOTE THAT REVEALED DEMOCRATS' NEW DIVIDE ON ISRAEL

He would become the nation’s first Muslim senator if elected.

As some Democrats grapple with the direction of their party following El-Sayed's nomination, Rogers said the "fight is far greater than just left versus right."

"The fight is for the very soul of our nation," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to El Sayed's campaign for comment.

item.title: Lindsey Graham's final mission to punish Putin clears Senate after yearlong fight
item.description: The sanctions bill targets Russia's oil and gas revenue with up to 500% tariffs on Russian imports and penalties on countries buying Russian energy.
item.content:encoded:
It’s taken well over a year of stops, starts, promises and derailments, but the Senate has at last advanced a bone-crushing package of sanctions against Russia, capping off one of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham’s biggest fights.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act sailed through the Senate on another colossal bipartisan vote and is now headed to the House. It has the backing of President Donald Trump, too.

It comes after personal lobbying from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy last week, who, hours after Graham’s memorial service in Washington, D.C., pleaded with lawmakers to put a check on Russian President Vladimir Putin.

GRAHAM'S FINAL MISSION ADVANCES AS SENATE MOVES TO CRUSH PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE WITH RUSSIA, IRAN SANCTIONS

"Today, President Zelenskyy is watching from Ukraine, and Putin is watching from Moscow," Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said on the Senate floor. "I would like to think that Lindsey Graham is watching, too."

The bill focuses on kneecapping Putin’s war machine by targeting Moscow’s top financial driver: oil and gas sales.

It also extends sanction authority against Iran that hampers funding to the country’s weapons and energy sectors as the administration and negotiators abroad seek to find a long-lasting peace agreement for the war in the Middle East.

There are also targeted sanctions against Putin, Russian officials and Russian military leaders, up to 500% tariffs on Russian imports, tariffs of up to 100% on the top five countries buying Russian energy, like China and India, and gives Trump flexibility for when to turn off some aspects of the sanctions.

'A BIG EFFING DEAL': GRAHAM'S FINAL MISSION MOVES FORWARD AFTER HIS DEATH

The tariff authority, however, threatened one last derailment of the package.

Sens. Rand Paul, R-Ky., and Ron Wyden, D-Ore., initially held up the package over the issue and offered an amendment to solve the problem.

Paul, who has staunchly opposed Trump’s tariff strategy since he retook office, argued that slapping tariffs on superpowers working with Russia, like China, would only cause them to cozy up.

"These tariffs threaten to undermine America's strategic position in the world," Paul said. "Some naively think that the tariffs will get China to distance themselves from Russia, but it might be the opposite."

TRUMP ALLIES PUSH TO ARM PRESIDENT WITH NEW TARIFF WEAPON TO PUNISH COUNTRIES 'RIPPING OFF' AMERICA

"Recent history suggests that they will instead push Russia and China together," he continued. "China is not going to get this 100% tariff and say, ‘Oh, we're sorry, we're no longer going to cooperate with Russia.’"

Then came Sen. Raphael Warnock, D-Ga., who proved to be the last hurdle.

But after meeting with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Thursday, Warnock backed down after receiving a commitment that Trump’s tariff authority was indeed limited to just the top five countries purchasing oil and gas exports from Russia.

"We should not have to choose between putting a check on Putin's aggression and putting a check on this president's tariff regime," Warnock said. "That is a false choice, and it is one that I am not willing to accept."

item.title: North Korea expert warns US can 'never take their eye off' Kim Jong Un following missile test during Iran war
item.description: A North Korea expert said the U.S. can never take its eye off Kim Jong Un and the Korean Peninsula after North Korea test-fired a missile this week.
item.content:encoded:
A North Korea expert told Fox News Digital that the United States "can never take their eye off" Kim Jong Un and the Korean Peninsula after Pyongyang test-fired a missile this week amid the ongoing conflict with Iran.

The launch of the short-range ballistic missile — which Japan said landed in the waters off North Korea’s east coast — unfolded Thursday ahead of joint military exercises to be conducted by the U.S. and South Korea later this month.

"There's this unsettled conflict on the Korean Peninsula. And Kim Jong Un, a very unpredictable leader that seeks attention, that is something the United States can never take their eye off," retired Navy Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery, a senior fellow at Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Friday.

"So we have all these challenges in the Middle East, these challenges with Russia and Ukraine, these challenges with China pressuring and trying to coerce Taiwan. You can never forget that the North Korean challenge to South Korea is sitting right there, and there are no constraints on Kim Jong Un," Montgomery added. "There's no version of an empowered elite or a population or a military that could unseat him. So we should always keep our eye on him, pay attention to him, and make sure we're constantly deterring any provocative behavior."

US SAYS NORTH KOREA MISSILE LAUNCH POSES NO IMMEDIATE THREAT, 'CONSULTING CLOSELY' WITH ALLIES

U.S. Indo-Pacific Command said following North Korea’s launch on Thursday that, "We are aware of the missile launch and are consulting closely with our allies and partners."

"Based on current assessments, this event does not pose an immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or to our allies," it added. "The United States remains committed to the defense of the U.S. homeland and our allies in the region."

Montgomery said Friday that "whenever North Korea does a ballistic missile launch, you have to think there's any of three countries that could be the intended recipient of the message — it could be the United States, it could be South Korea, it can be Japan or it could be a mix."

MORE THAN HALF OF SOME US WEAPONS STOCKPILES USED IN IRAN WAR, RAISING CONCERNS ABOUT CHINA THREAT

He described how Japan recently test-fired a Tomahawk cruise missile in late July, with the help of the U.S. Navy.

"Maybe this could be a signal back to them," Montgomery said. "South Korea and the United States are about to start the Ulchi Freedom series of exercises... the most robust series of exercise we have there every August when conducted."

Montgomery also said "recently there have been a lot of reports the United States has expended a large percentage of its theater ballistic missile defense weapons... Patriot 3 and THAAD, in the conflict in Iran."

"Those are the kind of defensive systems that might be used against this weapon. Also, there's U.S. Navy standard missiles, which also have been depleted in the Middle East. In all those cases, North Korea could be signaling to any of the three countries or a mix of the three countries that we're still relevant, we matter, and you need to pay attention to us," he said.

Fox News’ Liz Friden contributed to this report.

item.title: Smart toilet seat could detect AFib in 30 seconds
item.description: The HARO EKG-seat by Hamberger Medical records a six-lead EKG in 30 seconds while you sit, scanning for atrial fibrillation and irregular heartbeat.
item.content:encoded:
Your next bathroom break could come with an unexpected bonus: a check of your heart rhythm. German medical technology company Hamberger Medical has developed the HARO EKG-seat. It looks like a regular toilet seat, but built-in sensors record an electrocardiogram, also called an EKG or ECG, while you sit.

After about 30 seconds, a connected smartphone app analyzes the reading for signs of an irregular heart rhythm, including possible atrial fibrillation. AFib is the most common type of irregular heartbeat, and millions of people may have it without realizing anything feels wrong. It sounds like the kind of idea someone dreamed up during a very long bathroom break.

However, the possibility of catching a silent heart condition during something you already do every day deserves attention. Here's what the early research reveals about how well the seat works and where its limits begin.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

COULD A PAINT-ON ELECTRONIC TATTOO SPOT HEART ATTACKS?

A conventional medical EKG usually requires you to lie down while a medical professional places electrodes on your chest and other parts of your body. The HARO EKG-seat takes a different approach. Its sensors collect electrical signals from your body while you sit normally. The seat records a six-lead resting EKG and sends the information to its companion app through Bluetooth.

You do not need to attach sticky pads or remember to put on a wearable. You sit for about 30 seconds and let the seat do the work. Hamberger Medical says participants in its usability testing could operate the system without special instructions. The oldest participants in one reported study were in their 90s, according to published reports about the device. That simplicity may become one of its biggest strengths. Many health devices end up forgotten in a drawer after the novelty fades. A toilet seat is harder to forget.

The company tested the seat through what it calls the Hamberger Heart Study. Researchers compared the seat's six-lead EKG with a standard 12-lead medical EKG. Hamberger Medical reported a high level of agreement between the two systems when checking for AFib and other rhythm abnormalities.

That sounds encouraging, but there is an important limitation. The complete results have not been published in an independently peer-reviewed medical journal. Public reports also do not provide enough detail about the study's size, false alerts or performance across different groups.

Without those numbers, we cannot tell how often the seat might miss AFib or mistakenly warn someone whose heart rhythm is normal. For now, the results should be viewed as promising company-reported findings. They do not prove that the seat can replace a hospital EKG or a doctor's diagnosis.

AFib causes the heart's upper chambers to beat irregularly. Blood may then pool inside the heart, which can allow clots to form. A clot can travel to the brain and cause a stroke. The American Heart Association says AFib is linked to about five times the risk of stroke. Some people feel a racing heartbeat or fluttering in their chest. Others notice fatigue, dizziness or shortness of breath.

However, AFib can also arrive without obvious warning signs. A person may feel fine while the irregular rhythm comes and goes. That creates a detection problem. A brief EKG at a doctor's office may look normal if the AFib episode ended before the appointment. Doctors sometimes use longer-term monitors when they suspect an intermittent rhythm problem. A toilet seat that records readings regularly could provide more chances to capture an episode.

WEARABLE PATCH VIBRATES WHEN DANGER IS NEARBY

The American Heart Association estimates that about 5 million Americans currently live with AFib. It projects that more than 12 million could have the condition by 2030. Early detection can help doctors decide whether someone needs medication, additional monitoring or treatment to restore a normal rhythm.

Dr. Paari Dominic, a cardiac electrophysiologist, told the American Medical Association that earlier intervention can significantly improve outcomes. He noted that research supports pursuing normal rhythm within a year of detecting AFib in appropriate patients. However, a notification from a toilet seat should begin a medical conversation. It should never end one.

Age raises the likelihood of developing AFib. High blood pressure also plays a major role. Diabetes, obesity, sleep apnea and certain heart conditions can increase the risk. Smoking and excessive alcohol use may contribute as well.

Heavy drinking can sometimes trigger an irregular heartbeat even in people without a known heart condition. Doctors often call this "holiday heart syndrome" because cases can rise during celebrations involving heavier alcohol use. People who already face a higher risk could benefit most from convenient monitoring. That decision should involve a cardiologist or another qualified medical professional.

A heart-monitoring toilet seat collects highly sensitive information, so its privacy protections deserve a close look. According to Hamberger Medical's app privacy policy, EKG processing happens locally on the connected phone or tablet. The company says readings are not sent to its servers. The app also lets you export a PDF report. Hamberger Medical recommends protecting the file with a password before sending it to someone else. However, your phone's backup settings may still upload app information to iCloud or Google Backup. The company notes that this depends on how you configured your device.

Before using any connected health product, check its backup settings and sharing options. You should also protect your phone with a strong passcode. For additional steps, see our guide on how to stop health and fitness apps from using your private data.

HEART CONDITION TIED TO LINDSEY GRAHAM'S DEATH CAN STRIKE WITHOUT WARNING — WHAT TO KNOW

The HARO EKG-seat does not currently appear to be available for purchase. Hamberger Medical previously said the device was sold exclusively through its official German online shop at approximately $2,870. CyberGuy reached out to Hamberger Medical to confirm current availability, pricing and whether the company plans to sell the EKG-seat in the United States, but did not hear back before our deadline.

The HARO EKG-seat shows how health monitoring could blend into your normal routine. That part is genuinely promising. The clinical report suggests the seat can record EKGs that cardiologists interpret with strong accuracy. However, the current app results do not support relying on its automated AFib classification alone.

A normal app reading should not convince you to ignore symptoms. An abnormal warning should lead to a conversation with a medical professional. Contact your doctor if you notice a racing or irregular heartbeat, recurring dizziness or unexplained shortness of breath. Chest pain or pressure may signal a medical emergency, so call 911 right away. Never start or stop heart medication because of a consumer device result. Your doctor may order a clinical EKG or longer-term monitoring before making a diagnosis.

There is something undeniably clever about turning an ordinary toilet seat into a heart monitor. It fits health screening into a routine that people already follow without reminders. The company-reported results sound encouraging, especially for a condition that may hide between doctor visits. Smart health technology works best when it helps you notice a concern sooner and gives your doctor useful information. It becomes dangerous when a gadget creates false confidence or replaces professional care.

Would you trust a smart toilet seat with your heart data if it could uncover a silent problem before your next doctor visit? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.
